**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the SVG when queueing feedback**

When the user clicks **Queue feedback**, `whiteboard-frame.js` creates the persistence payload without the new third `svg` argument, and `queueWhiteboardFeedback` then passes that message to `saveWhiteboardScene`. This coercion consequently sends `svg: ""` and overwrites the valid SVG produced by the preceding autosave, leaving the approved state without the snapshot this change is intended to preserve. Generate or carry the SVG in the queue-feedback payload as well.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize SVG generation before posting saves**

If another edit or flush starts while an autosave's `exportToSvg` is still pending, the `postSave` calls run concurrently. Because each scene is posted only after its own export resolves, a newer export can finish first and an older captured scene can arrive afterward; the chrome save chain preserves that arrival order, so the stale scene and SVG become the final persisted state. Serialize these exports or discard superseded completions so autosave ordering remains monotonic.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep SVG export outside the bounded reload flush**

During a version-driven chrome reload, the existing flush path waits only 1.5 seconds, but it now cannot even post the scene until this potentially expensive SVG export finishes. For a complex diagram whose export exceeds that window, the chrome reloads and destroys the frame before the save request starts, losing the latest edits; persist the scene first or use a previously generated snapshot so the bounded flush can still complete.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid exceeding the whiteboard write limit with duplicated assets**

For scenes containing a large embedded image, the scene already carries its data URL in `files`, while `exportToSvg` embeds the same image again in the SVG. Including both in this request can push a previously accepted scene-only payload over the route's fixed 20 MB JSON limit—for example, an image around 10–20 MB—causing every autosave to return 413. Store the snapshot separately, raise the limit appropriately, or otherwise avoid duplicating large binary data in one request.
